study_identification_part.si_4_title: A neuroimaging measure to capture heterogeneous patterns of atrophy in Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used warped Bayesian Linear Regression (WBLR) with likelihood warping to model normative lifespan curves for cortical thicknesses and subcortical volumes. The reference normative model from Rutherford et al. (2022) was applied, which uses Bayesian linear regression with likelihood warping. All modelling steps were performed using PCNToolkit (v0.20).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Rutherford and colleagues (Rutherford et al., 2022) modelled normative lifespan curves for cortical thicknesses across 148 regions (Destrieux parcellation) and subcortical volumes derived from Freesurfer using a warped Bayesian Linear Regression with age and sex as covariates, and accounting for site differences (Bayer et al., 2022). Bayesian linear regression with likelihood warping allows accurate modelling of non-Gaussian effects and upscaling of normative models to large cohorts (Fraza et al., 2021).

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled cortical thickness values (148 regions from Destrieux parcellation) and subcortical volumes (21 regions) derived from T1-weighted MRI scans processed with FreeSurfer. The total of 169 brain regions (148 cortical + 21 subcortical) were used to calculate z-scores and identify outliers.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Cortical thickness values (Destrieux parcellation; lh.aparc.a2009s.stats, rh.aparc.a2009s.stats) (Destrieux et al., 2010) and subcortical volumes (aseg.stats) were extracted. [...] The total number of outliers across the 169 regions (148 cortical and 21 subcortical) was summed per participant to provide the total outlier count.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model used age and sex as covariates for modeling the lifespan curves. Site differences were accounted for through an adapted transfer learning approach that recalibrated the reference normative model to the study datasets by inputting control data from the two study sites.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: Rutherford and colleagues (Rutherford et al., 2022) modelled normative lifespan curves for cortical thicknesses across 148 regions (Destrieux parcellation) and subcortical volumes derived from Freesurfer using a warped Bayesian Linear Regression with age and sex as covariates, and accounting for site differences (Bayer et al., 2022). [...] The reference normative model was recalibrated to the study datasets with an adapted transfer learning approach (Kia et al., 2022). This involved inputting control data from our two study sites into the reference normative model to generate stable parameters for cortical thicknesses and subcortical volumes, to account for residual differences in data distributions, caused by factors such as scanner differences.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Bhome2024.pdf.md: Section 2.4 Reference normative dataset; Section 2.5 Applying neuroimaging normative modelling to study data
